title: Sea otters protect underwater forests by eating sea urchins
body: Sea urchins graze on kelp, and when nothing keeps them in check they can multiply and strip kelp forests down to bare rock. Sea otters eat large numbers of urchins, which lets kelp grow back and shelter fish and countless other species. Because a single predator shapes an entire ecosystem far out of proportion to its numbers, the sea otter is a textbook example of what ecologists call a keystone species.

slides.heading: First to last: when the otters vanish
items: Kelp is grazed down to bare rock
slides.explanation: Urchins graze kelp. With no otters to eat them, they multiply and strip the forest to bare rock, so the fish and other species sheltering in it lose their home.

slides.heading: How otters keep the kelp standing

steps.label: Sea otters eat lots of sea urchins
Fewer urchins are left to graze the kelp
Fish and many other species find shelter

slides.question: In what year did the first international treaty halt the hunting of sea otters for their fur?
slides.explanation: 1911: Russia, Japan, Britain and the US signed a treaty with a moratorium on hunting sea otters; by then an estimated 1,000–2,000 were left. A 1972 US law later made hunting them illegal.

slides.heading: Remove the otter
slides.text: Fur hunting from 1741 to 1911 cut sea otters to roughly 1,000–2,000 animals. Where they vanished, urchin numbers could boom and kelp forests suffered.

slides.heading: Bring it back
slides.text: After a hunting ban and reintroductions, otters returned to much of their range. Where they recovered, urchins declined and kelp could regrow.

slides.heading: No blubber needed
slides.text: Unlike seals and whales, sea otters have no thick blubber layer. They stay warm with the densest fur in the animal kingdom.
